title: You will die, and they will die too.
subtitle: The one appointment no one misses
then: Ibn Kathir notes this is one of the verses {idea}Abu Bakr recited when the Prophet ﷺ died{/idea}, so people would accept that he had truly passed. Even the best of creation would taste death.
now: You argue with a relative for years over an inheritance, a slight, a wedding seating plan. Both of you act as if there is all the time in the world. {idea}You will die. They will die.{/idea} Then what was it all for?
old: Death is something that happens to other people, later.
new: Death came even to the Prophet ﷺ, so I should live each day as if I will stand before Allah.
try: Think of one quarrel you are holding onto, and ask if it would matter at your funeral.

title: Every unsettled dispute will be reopened before your Lord.
subtitle: Arguments do not end at the grave
then: When this was revealed, Az-Zubayr asked if their wrongs against others would be repeated. The Prophet ﷺ said {idea}yes, until everyone gets their right back.{/idea} Az-Zubayr said: by Allah, this is a very serious matter.
now: The money you borrowed and never mentioned again. The coworker whose credit you took. The harsh words to your mother. {trap}They are not closed.{/trap} {reward}You can settle them here, while it is still easy.{/reward}
old: Old wrongs fade if nobody brings them up.
new: Every right will be restored before Allah, so I should return what I owe now.
try: Settle one small debt or wrong today: pay it back, give credit, or apologize.

title: Lying about Allah and rejecting truth: the double wrong.
subtitle: Who could be more unjust
then: Ibn Kathir says the idolaters claimed Allah had partners and daughters, then rejected the truth brought by the Messengers. {trap}They combined both falsehoods{/trap}, which is why no one does more wrong.
now: Someone shows you clear proof you were wrong. You feel the sting, and the easy move is to twist the facts and dismiss them. {idea}The test is what you do when truth reaches you.{/idea}
old: If I don't like what the truth says, I can just ignore it.
new: Rejecting truth once it reaches me is among the greatest wrongs.
try: Think of one point someone made that you brushed off. Reconsider it honestly today.

title: The one who brought the truth, and those who believed it.
subtitle: Bringing truth and accepting it

key.label: The contrast with the last verse

then: Mujahid and others said the one who brought the truth is {idea}the Messenger ﷺ{/idea}, and those who believed in it are the Muslims. Ibn Abbas said they are the ones who {idea}fear and shun shirk.{/idea}
now: Someone says something true at the family dinner and the table goes quiet. You know they are right. You can stay silent, or be the one who says: yes, that is true. {reward}Confirming truth is its own good deed.{/reward}
old: Only the one who speaks up first gets credit.
new: Believing and backing the truth when it comes is also taqwa.
try: Next time someone says something true and unpopular, quietly back them up.

title: Whatever they wish for, with their Lord.
subtitle: The reward of the doers of good
then: Ibn Kathir explains it is in Paradise: {reward}whatever they ask for, they will have.{/reward} It is called the reward of the muhsinin, those who do good.
now: Your wish list grows every month: a better car, a bigger place, a holiday. Every wish met makes room for a new one. {reward}There is a place where wanting finally rests.{/reward}
old: I will be happy once I get the next thing I want.
new: The wishes that are fully met are kept with my Lord for those who do good.
try: Delete one item from your shopping cart today and give its price, or part of it, in charity.

title: Your worst erased, your best becomes the measure.
subtitle: How Allah rewards the doers of good
then: Ibn Kathir links it to the verse about people whose {reward}best deeds are accepted and whose evil deeds are overlooked.{/reward} This is the reward for those who brought and confirmed the truth.
now: You keep replaying the worst thing you ever did, the night you would undo if you could. It feels like the headline of your life. {reward}For those who turn to Him and do good, the worst is erased and the best is the measure.{/reward}
old: My worst mistake is who I really am.
new: Allah can wipe my worst and pay me by the measure of my best.
try: Do one good deed today with full effort, the kind you would want to be measured by.

title: Is Allah not enough for His servant?
subtitle: When they try to frighten you

row.title: the idols
sub: used to scare the Prophet ﷺ

row.title: Allah suffices
sub: for the one who relies on Him

then: Ibn Kathir says the idolaters {trap}tried to scare the Messenger ﷺ with their idols.{/trap} The reply is a question: {idea}is Allah not sufficient for His servant?{/idea} Some read it as His servants, covering all who rely on Him.
now: A manager hints your contract may not be renewed. A relative warns that people will talk. Fear sits in your chest at 3am. {idea}Is Allah not enough for you?{/idea}
old: I need to cover every angle myself or I am unsafe.
new: Allah is enough for the one who worships Him and relies on Him.
try: When a fear comes up today, say hasbunallah and name the fear to Him.

title: Whom Allah guides, no one can mislead.
subtitle: Guidance that cannot be taken away

row.title: Allah guides
sub: the one who turns to Him

then: Ibn Kathir explains that {idea}whoever relies on Him and turns to Him will never be forsaken{/idea}, for He is the Almighty whom no one can overwhelm. This came while the Prophet ﷺ faced threats in Makkah.
now: You worry that the new job, the new city, the new friends will pull you away from your deen. You feel fragile. {reward}Stay turned toward Him{/reward}, and no crowd can pull out what He placed.
old: My faith could be taken from me at any time by the wrong people.
new: When I keep turning to Allah, no one can mislead what He guides.
try: Ask Allah today, in your own words, to keep your heart firm on His way.

title: No one can lift His harm or hold back His mercy.
subtitle: Sufficient for me is Allah
then: The idolaters admitted Allah created the heavens and earth, yet called on others. Ibn Kathir cites the Prophet's ﷺ words: {idea}if the whole nation gathered to harm you, they could not, except what Allah decreed.{/idea}
now: You keep checking the job portal, refreshing the inbox, calling the friend with connections. {trap}As if they decide.{/trap} Do your part, then rest: {reward}if He wills mercy, no one can block it.{/reward}
old: My outcome depends on the right people saying yes.
new: No one can stop a mercy Allah sends, so I rely on Him and do my part.
try: After doing all you can for one worry today, say hasbiyallahu alayhi tawakkaltu and let it go.

title: Do your work, I will do mine. You will see.
subtitle: Staying on your way under pressure
then: Ibn Kathir calls it {trap}a threat and a warning{/trap} to those who opposed. The surah introduction says the Prophet ﷺ was to tell them their persecution would never deter him; {idea}he would continue his mission.{/idea}
now: Your friends mock your choice not to drink at the office party. You could argue all night. Or you smile, drink your juice, and keep living your way. {idea}Time shows whose way was wise.{/idea}
old: I need to convince everyone that I am right.
new: I keep doing what is right and leave the outcome to show itself.
try: Next time your faith is mocked, do not argue. Stay kind and stay the course.

title: Disgrace here, and a lasting punishment after.
subtitle: The end the warning points to
then: Ibn Kathir says the disgracing torment comes {trap}in this world{/trap} and the enduring one on the Day of Resurrection. He ends: {idea}we seek refuge with Allah from that.{/idea}
now: You read a warning like this and quickly think of someone else who deserves it. {idea}Turn it inward.{/idea} Which part of my own way of living would I not want to bring before Him?
old: Warnings like this are for the really bad people.
new: Every warning is a chance for me to seek refuge and fix my own path.
try: Say a'udhu billah sincerely once today and mean it for yourself.

title: Guidance benefits you; straying harms only you.
subtitle: The messenger is not a guard over people
then: Ibn Kathir explains the Book is for all of creation, and {idea}the benefit of guidance returns to the one guided.{/idea} The Prophet ﷺ was told he is not responsible for guiding them; his duty is to convey.
now: You pray, you fast, you give, and part of you thinks you are doing Allah a favor. Or you skip it all and think it only affects your mood. {idea}It all comes back to you.{/idea}
old: My worship is something I do for Allah's sake only, as a favor.
new: Every step of guidance benefits my own soul, and every step away harms it.
try: Before your next prayer, tell yourself: this is for my own soul.

title: Every night He takes your soul, and most mornings returns it.
subtitle: Sleep as a small death

row.title: a return
sub: my soul sent back to me

then: Ibn Kathir describes sleep as a lesser death. The Prophet ﷺ taught a bedtime dua: {idea}if You take my soul, have mercy on it, and if You send it back, protect it.{/idea}
now: You fall asleep scrolling, phone on your face. You wake to an alarm and reach for it again. {reward}Your soul was taken and handed back.{/reward} That deserves more than a groan.
old: Waking up every day is just normal.
new: Every waking is my soul returned to me, a new term granted by Allah.
try: Tonight, before sleep, say: In Your name, my Lord, I lie down, and in Your name I rise.

title: Intercessors that own nothing and understand nothing.
subtitle: Whom do you rely on to speak for you
then: Ibn Kathir says they took idols {trap}on the basis of their own whims, with no evidence.{/trap} These cannot think, hear, or see, yet they were expected to plead before Allah.
now: You carry a lucky charm to the interview. You trust your family name to get you through. You think your title will speak for you someday. {idea}Ask what it actually owns.{/idea}
old: Something or someone will put in a good word for me.
new: Things that own nothing cannot speak for me before Allah.
try: Notice one object or habit you treat as a good-luck guarantee, and let it go today.

title: All intercession belongs to Allah alone.
subtitle: No one speaks without His permission

row.title: by His leave
sub: for whom He is pleased with

then: Ibn Kathir explains that intercession {idea}avails only for one Allah is pleased with, by His permission.{/idea} He cites the Throne Verse: who can intercede with Him except by His leave?
now: You hope that being near pious people will be enough: the right mosque, the right circle, the scholar friend. Good company helps. {idea}But the one to please is Allah Himself.{/idea}
old: Being close to good people will cover me.
new: All intercession is His to grant, so my effort goes to pleasing Him.
try: Do one act today purely to please Allah, not to be seen near anyone.
